transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-06-18
Time: 16:00 PT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Marco Alvarez (Redwood AE), Jenna Park (Redwood SE), Rajesh 'Raj' Kumar (CTO, Orion), Priya Nair (Head of Security, Orion), Liam O'Connor (SRE Lead, Orion)

Summary: Security posture discovery to understand compliance requirements and deployment options — hosted API vs dedicated vs private (VPC/on-prem).

[00:00] Marco: Hey everyone thanks for joining, I'm Marco from Redwood, I'm the account lead. With me is Jenna, our solutions engineer.
[00:08] Jenna: Hi all, hi Raj, Priya, Liam, thanks for the time. We wanted to run through your compliance posture and map that to Redwood's hosted, dedicated, and private options.
[00:18] Raj: Hi, thanks. Quick note — we're evaluating a few vendors, but security is the gating factor. We want to understand SOC2/ISO coverage, SSO, RBAC, and encryption. Also where logs live and retention.
[00:28] Priya: Yeah, we have strict data residency for EU customers, BYOK for keys, and audit log forwarding to our SIEM (we use Splunk). We also need a preserved chain for access reviews.
[00:41] Marco: Great. Jenna, want to start with attestation and compliance?
[00:44] Jenna: Sure. At a high level, Redwood is SOC 2 Type II compliant and we also maintain ISO27001 certification. We can provide the attestation reports under an NDA. For hosted customers we have SOC2 controls that cover logical and physical security, change management, and incident response. (note: automated transcript sometimes reads "soc too" or "sock two").
[01:05] Priya: Are those full scope for inference workloads and also for Dedicated/Private? In other words, if we move to Dedicated pools or Private VPC, do we still see the same attestation scope?
[01:15] Jenna: Good question. The SOC2/ISO scope covers the Redwood control plane and hosted infra. For Dedicated, we provide a dedicated GPU pool in a segregated tenancy and the contract includes SLAs; the attestation still covers Redwood's operational controls managing that environment. For Private (VPC or on-prem), some controls shift to customer responsibility — e.g., network segmentation, customer-managed KMS — so we clarify shared responsibility in the security docs.
[01:41] Raj: Can you be explicit about BYOK or customer-managed keys? We prefer HSM-backed keys and we need encryption at rest with keys we control.
[01:49] Jenna: Absolutely. We support Bring Your Own Key (BYOK) for both Dedicated and Private deployments. For Hosted customers we offer Redwood-managed KMS by default, but we can integrate with customer KMS (Azure Key Vault, AWS KMS, or on-prem HSM) for enterprise plans. If you require HSM-only, that's typically in the Private/on-prem offering where your KMS is inside your network.
[02:10] Liam: For the hosted option, if you integrate with our KMS, does any key material leave our environment?
[02:16] Jenna: No, the key material remains in your KMS/HSM. Redwood sends envelope-encrypted payloads — we don't store your plaintext key. There are some implementation details we can run through in the deep dive.
[02:27] Priya: Audit logs — we need write-once retention and the ability to forward to Splunk and also retain for 7 years for certain regs. What does Redwood provide?
[02:36] Marco: Redwood captures granular audit logs — API calls, token usage, model changes, admin activity. We support forwarding to SIEMs via connectors (S3 bucket delivery or direct forwarders). Retention is configurable and we offer long-term archive options for enterprise customers.
[02:49] Jenna: In Hosted, we keep operational logs for our internal SRE but can set up customer log delivery to your accounts. For Dedicated and Private, logs can be configured to live in your environment for full control.
[03:01] Raj: How about RBAC and SSO? We need role separation and SAML SSO; ideally SCIM for provisioning.
[03:06] Jenna: Redwood supports SSO via SAML and OIDC. We also support SCIM for user provisioning. RBAC is configurable with roles — admin, developer, read-only, billing — and you can set per-route/model permissions. On Private deployments RBAC hooks into your identity provider for enterprise SSO and we support attribute-based access controls.
[03:24] Priya: Any known limitations around per-model access controls? For example, allowing only a set of teams to call production models and others only to run evals.
[03:33] Jenna: Yes, we have per-model and per-route access controls. There's an ability to create environment tags and route policies; sometimes in the hosted product very granular controls require enterprise plans but Dedicated/Private has full parity. We'll document exact capabilities in the follow-up.
[03:48] Liam: Network controls — can the dedicated pools be in our VPC or do they sit in Redwood-managed accounts?
[03:54] Marco: Dedicated pools can be configured in a few ways: Redwood-managed accounts with network peering, or customer VPC peering depending on cloud provider. For stricter network controls we recommend Private (VPC or on-prem) where the control plane is customer-visible. Jenna will share diagrams.
[04:11] Priya: Data residency — we need EU-only processing for EU customers. How do you guarantee it's not routed through US regions?
[04:19] Jenna: We support region pinning for requests and model hosting. For Hosted customers we have regional endpoints in EU and we can pin traffic. For Dedicated, you can reserve capacity in a specific region. For Private on-prem, obviously it's local. We'll be explicit about cross-region fallbacks — we advise disabling automatic cross-region fallback if compliance prohibits it.
[04:39] Raj: Incident response and breach notification SLAs?
[04:43] Marco: We have an incident response program; for enterprise contracts we include notification timelines in the SLA. SOC2 reports and penetration test summaries can be provided under NDA.
[04:54] Priya: Pen test evidence — do you do third-party pen tests and can we get the summary?
[04:59] Jenna: Yes, we do regular third-party pen tests. We can provide executive summaries and remediation timelines under NDA. Full reports typically require a client-specific NDA.
[05:10] Marco: Quick note — some of the transcript Automatic captioning might read "KV cache" as "K V cash" or "K V cache" — apologies if the transcript looks odd.
[05:20] Raj: No worries. On the compliance questionnaire front, we have a 50‑page RFP that goes to vendors; will Redwood fill that out?
[05:27] Marco: We do; our security team can help. Jenna, what's the expected turnaround?
[05:30] Jenna: Typically 5–7 business days for the questionnaire and we can prioritize sections if you highlight high-risk areas.
[05:36] Priya: We also need evidence of separation of duties and privileged access reviews. How does Redwood handle admin accounts?
[05:44] Jenna: Admin access is controlled through RBAC and we require MFA for privileged accounts. We rotate service account keys, and there are approval workflows for escalations. We can provide screenshots of the admin audit logs and process docs.
[05:56] Liam: For runtime isolation, do you co-locate other tenants on the same GPU or do you schedule across tenants?
[06:03] Jenna: In Hosted, multi-tenant scheduling is used to maximize utilization, but we have strict isolation at process level. For Dedicated you get a pool reserved for your workloads — no other tenant runs there. For Private, it's fully under your control.
[06:18] Raj: Any data leakage risks via caching (KV cache) across requests? We need assurance that one customer's prefix cache doesn't bleed into another's.
[06:27] Jenna: Good point. We have tenant isolation on KV/cache layers; caches are namespaced and encrypted. For extra assurance we can disable shared caching for sensitive workloads or run Dedicated/Private where cache is not shared.
[06:41] Priya: What about model artifacts — are models considered customer data? If we fine-tune or upload proprietary models, where do they live and who can access them?
[06:50] Marco: Uploaded models and fine-tunes are stored in project-scoped storage and access is controlled via RBAC. For Private deployments, model artifacts can live inside your VPC or on-prem storage. We treat them as customer assets and document retention and deletion flows.
[07:05] Raj: Regulatory — GDPR data subject requests pipeline. If a user asks for deletion, what's the flow?
[07:11] Jenna: We support data deletion requests; there are different layers — request logs, training data, and model artifacts. We can show the lifecycle and typical timelines; for some internal logs we may need to redact or archive per contract. We'll include the policy in the follow-up.
[07:25] Priya: Do you provide periodic auditor access or cooperation for customer audits?
[07:30] Marco: Yes, enterprise agreements include audit cooperation clauses. We can support SOC engagements where auditors need to review controls. Specific access levels are part of contracting.
[07:40] Raj: Integration with SIEM — is there an out-of-the-box Splunk connector or we need to build something?
[07:45] Jenna: We have S3 delivery plus direct connectors for popular SIEMs including Splunk and Datadog. For Splunk, we can forward logs via HTTP Event Collector or use S3 ingestion depending on your architecture.
[07:58] Liam: For log integrity we want WORM-style storage for some logs. Is that supported?
[08:03] Jenna: Yes, we support WORM-style retention via S3 Object Lock or equivalent archive features for enterprise archiving.
[08:12] Priya: A couple of commercial/security constraints: we can't have vendor support staff access customer data unless it's under a jump box and logged. How does Redwood handle support access?
[08:22] Marco: Support access is role-based and requires approval for any privileged sessions. For sensitive customers we set up bastion/jump boxes with session recording and customer approval.
[08:33] Raj: Great. Can you provide an architecture diagram showing control plane vs data plane separation?
[08:38] Jenna: Yes — we'll include diagrams for Hosted, Dedicated, and Private and highlight which controls are customer-managed.
[08:46] Priya: Also want to confirm that model telemetry that we send (usage, latencies, errors) doesn't include PII by default.
[08:54] Jenna: Default telemetry is metadata-level and doesn't include request content unless you opt into sending samples for quality monitoring. We redact or hash sensitive fields by default in our telemetry pipeline.
[09:07] Marco: At this point, what's your tilt — are you more likely to go Hosted with enterprise controls, or Dedicated/Private?
[09:12] Raj: We would prefer Hosted if it meets our BYOK and EU residency constraints; otherwise Dedicated or Private. Cost and time-to-production also matter.
[09:21] Priya: Compliance and auditability are the top two criteria; perf and cost are second. If Hosted can meet our compliance checklist, that's ideal.
[09:29] Jenna: That maps well — we'll prioritize the hosted control options that satisfy BYOK and regional pinning and show the gap vs Dedicated/Private.
[09:39] Marco: OK, a few housekeeping items — I'll send the SOC2/ISO artifacts under NDA, Jenna will prepare the VPC/on-prem architecture and KMS integration options, and Priya will share the compliance RFP.
[09:52] Priya: Sounds good. Also include any sample contracts or data processing addendum (DPA).
[09:57] Marco: We'll include the DPA template.
[10:00] Raj: On timelines — we want to run a pilot as soon as next month. What does Redwood need to kick off a trial?
[10:07] Marco: We'll need an internal pilot project scope, test dataset (anonymized) and target evaluation metrics (latency, throughput, cost). We can provision Dedicated trial capacity for two weeks or a Hosted sandbox with region pinning.
[10:22] Liam: For benchmarking, can you support a sample test harness that hits token-level throughput?
[10:27] Jenna: Yes — we can provide a small benchmarking harness and coordinate load tests with your SRE. We'll create a spreadsheet to capture test scenarios.
[10:36] Priya: One last security question — do you have a documented data retention policy for logs and model artifacts and a process for deletion verification?
[10:45] Jenna: Yes, we have retention policies configurable per project. We'll include the retention matrix and deletion verification steps in the follow-up.
[10:55] Marco: Ok let's wrap with next steps and owners — Marco will send docs, Jenna will prepare diagrams and test harness, Priya will share RFP. Any questions?
[11:05] Priya: No, that's all for now. Thanks.
[11:08] Marco: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the artifacts and schedule the deep dive.
[11:12] (meeting ends)

Notes: Transcript contains occasional auto-caption errors (e.g., "Deicated" for "Dedicated", "sock two" for "SOC 2", "K V cache" for "KV cache"). Links referenced: security pack (link to be sent), architecture_diagram_deck.pdf (will be shared), benchmarking_spreadsheet.xlsx (will be shared).
